meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'more', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: В метро деньги ещё незаметнее вытащат.
examples.trans: On the metro they will steal the money even more unnoticeably.

examples.text: У меня, кстати, тоже хорошие новости.
examples.trans: By the way, I also have good news.

вытащить.gloss: to pull out, to get out

meanings.en: to pull out, to get out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (root 'тащить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to pull out', forming an aspectual pair with 'вытаскивать'.

examples.text: В метро деньги ещё незаметнее вытащат.
examples.trans: On the metro they will steal the money even more unnoticeably.

examples.text: Я тебя вытащу.
examples.trans: I'll get you out.

examples.text: Он вытащил телефон.
examples.trans: He pulled out his phone.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('let') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Пусть лучше Виктор Петрович будет су-шефом.
examples.trans: Let Viktor Petrovich be the sous-chef instead.

examples.text: Пусть деньги лучше полежат у меня.
examples.trans: Let the money rather stay with me for safekeeping.

examples.text: Ладно, пусть пока полежат у тебя.
examples.trans: All right, let it stay with you for now.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'better'.

examples.text: Пойду лучше спокойно покурю на улице.
examples.trans: I will rather go calmly have a smoke outside.

examples.text: Пусть лучше Виктор Петрович будет су-шефом.
examples.trans: Let Viktor Petrovich be the sous-chef instead.

examples.text: Пусть деньги лучше полежат у меня.
examples.trans: Let the money rather stay with me for safekeeping.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'stay', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Пусть деньги лучше полежат у меня.
examples.trans: Let the money rather stay with me for safekeeping.

examples.text: Ладно, пусть пока полежат у тебя.
examples.trans: All right, let it stay with you for now.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'when'.

examples.text: Когда квартиру найдёшь, сразу их заберёшь.
examples.trans: When you find an apartment, you will take it right back.

examples.text: Парни, я когда услышал, просто обомлел!
examples.trans: Guys, when I heard this, I was simply stunned!

examples.text: Скажи честно, когда нам понизят зарплату?
examples.trans: Tell us honestly, when will they lower our salary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('they') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Когда квартиру найдёшь, сразу их заберёшь.
examples.trans: When you find an apartment, you will take it right back.

examples.text: Они строят центр.
examples.trans: They are building a centre.

examples.text: Их накажет история.
examples.trans: History will punish them.

забрать.gloss: to take back, to take away

meanings.en: to take back, to take away
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (root 'брать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to take back', forming an aspectual pair with 'забирать'.

examples.text: Когда квартиру найдёшь, сразу их заберёшь.
examples.trans: When you find an apartment, you will take it right back.

examples.text: Он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: He will withdraw the statement.

examples.text: Я заберу ключи.
examples.trans: I'll take the keys.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('all right') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ладно, пусть пока полежат у тебя.
examples.trans: All right, let it stay with you for now.

examples.text: Ладно, уже иду, зачем так орать?
examples.trans: Fine, I am going already, why yell like that?

examples.text: Ладно, я уже ухожу к себе домой.
examples.trans: Fine, I am already heading home to my place.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'for now'.

examples.text: Ладно, пусть пока полежат у тебя.
examples.trans: All right, let it stay with you for now.

examples.text: Об этом пока ещё никто не знает.
examples.trans: Nobody knows about this yet.

examples.text: Куй железо, пока оно ещё горячо!
examples.trans: Strike while the iron is still hot!
